I1.name: the two-step energy ledger and the reference Euler schemes
I1.definition: State and forces are the 3-D kernel's (makeState, accelerations, energy). Schemes: 'explicit-euler' (x += h v_old, v += h a(x_old); the labelled reference, in no engine table), 'symplectic-euler' (v += h a(x), then x += h v_new), 'velocity-verlet' (the kernel's leapfrog, kick-drift-kick), 'rk4' (the kernel's). ledger(bodies, scheme, {h, span}) takes steps = round(span / h) steps (refused under 8) and returns the relative energy error eps_k = (E_k - E_0) / |E_0| summarised as end (eps at the last step) and maxAbs (max |eps_k|), the separation of bodies 0 and 1 at start and end, and unbound = true with the step index when E_k >= 0 for a system that began bound. twoStep runs h and h / 2 over the same span and returns ratioEnd = end(h) / end(h/2), ratioMax = maxAbs(h) / maxAbs(h/2), orderEnd = log2 |ratioEnd|, orderMax = log2 ratioMax, kind = 'secular' when |end| >= 0.5 maxAbs in both runs and 'oscillating' otherwise; for 'oscillating' orderEnd is null with reason 'end-phase'. Refusals: 'too-few-steps', 'unbound' (either run), 'rounding-floor' (maxAbs of the finer run below 1e-13). A non-finite or non-positive h or span, or an unknown scheme, throws RangeError.
I1.system: two bodies, m0 = 0.75, m1 = 0.25, G = 1, relative orbit with semi-major axis 1 and eccentricity e started at periapsis in the barycentric frame; period P = 2 pi

I2.name: the step history of the adaptive integrator
I2.definition: stepHistory(bodies, span, {tol, h0 = 0.001}) runs the kernel's dopri5 unchanged with its onStep and records, per accepted step, the time at its end, the step h and the separation r of bodies 0 and 1; it returns accepted, rejected, evaluations = 1 + 6 (accepted + rejected), hMin and hMax with the time and separation of each, the least-squares slope of ln h on ln r over the accepted steps, and the final positions. Refusal: 'step-collapse' when an accepted step is shorter than span * 1e-12 (the run stops there and returns the time, step and separation it stopped at), 'step-budget' when accepted + rejected reaches 200000. costAtEqualError(bodies, span, {tol}) takes as reference the same integrator at tol / 1000, the adaptive error as the largest absolute difference of a position coordinate from it at the end, then the smallest N = 2^k (k from 4 to 22) for which the kernel's fixed-step RK4 with N steps has an error against the same reference no larger; it returns errAdaptive, fixedSteps, fixedEvaluations = 4 N, adaptiveEvaluations and their ratio, or the refusal 'no-fixed-step'. tol or span non-positive or non-finite, or fewer than two bodies, throws RangeError.

I3.definition: ensembleRate(seriesList, {level = 0.9}) passes each pair's separation series [{t, d}] to js/chaos/divergence.js analyzeDivergence unchanged (its CRITERIA: 3 e-folds, 10 points, R^2 0.98 in the log domain, 2 e-folding times in the window, floor 1e-12, window from 1.5 times the first separation to 0.2 of the largest). It returns n, the count of each behaviour, and, when at least 10 pairs and at least half of the pairs are 'exponential', the estimate: the median rate, the bounds lo and hi (the (1 - level) / 2 and (1 + level) / 2 quantiles of the exponential pairs' rates, linear interpolation between order statistics, numpy's default), the median e-folding time 1 / median rate, the median R^2 and the window (the median 'from' and 'to' of the exponential pairs). The bounds are the spread of the pairs' finite-window rates, stated as such: not a confidence interval and not a Lyapunov exponent's error. Otherwise it refuses: 'too-few-pairs' (n under 10) or 'not-exponential' with the most frequent behaviour of the pairs that were not exponential (ties broken in the order identical, bounded, linear, saturated, insufficient) and the counts. threeBodyPair(realm, buildScenario, applyLab, seed, {delta = 1e-8, every = 10}) builds A8b's trial for a seed twice (the three-body kind's setup with physics 'validation-lab', its 1000 steps of 0.05 s, the draws of stream('experiments', seed)), the second with star 0's x moved by delta * 50 after the draws, and returns d(t) = sqrt(sum_i |r_i^A - r_i^B|^2) by index at t = 0 and after every 10th step (101 samples), with run A's relative energy drift.

I4.name: a discrete Fourier periodogram for a small series
I4.definition: fourierPeriodogram(t, y, {fmin, fmax, n}) subtracts the mean of y and, at each of n trial frequencies evenly spaced from fmin to fmax inclusive, forms C = sum (y - mean) cos(2 pi f t) and S = sum (y - mean) sin(2 pi f t) and the power P = 2 (C^2 + S^2) / (N sum (y - mean)^2), which is 1 for a sinusoid sampled evenly over whole cycles. It returns the grid, the peak (the largest grid power, its frequency refined by the parabola through it and its two neighbours, the period 1 / frequency, the amplitude 2 sqrt(C^2 + S^2) / N at the grid maximum), the resolution 1 / T with T = max t - min t, the full width at half the peak's power (linear interpolation on the grid; null when a half-power crossing is outside the grid), and the second peak: the largest local maximum of the grid more than one resolution from the peak. Refusals: 'too-few' (fewer than 8 points), 'no-variation' (sum (y - mean)^2 = 0), 'alias' when the second peak's power is at least 0.9 of the peak's (both frequencies returned, neither called the period). Warning 'coarse-grid' when the grid step exceeds half the resolution. Non-finite t or y, unequal lengths, fmin not positive, fmax not above fmin, n under 3 or N * n above 2,000,000 throws RangeError.

I5.name: the error of interpolating a table, at points left out
I5.definition: heldOut(xs, ys, {limit}) needs at least 5 points, xs finite and strictly increasing, ys finite. For each interior index k = 1 to n - 2 it removes point k, evaluates js/numeric/interp.js linear and cubicSpline (natural) of the remaining n - 1 points at xs[k], and records the two errors (predicted minus the held-out value) and the gap xs[k+1] - xs[k-1]. It returns the points, per method the root mean square and the largest absolute error, and closer = 'linear' or 'spline' (the smaller RMS; 'tie' when they differ by at most 1e-9 of the larger, or both are at most 1e-12). With a limit (the error the use tolerates, in the units of y) it refuses 'too-coarse' when both RMS errors exceed it, returning the errors and no recommendation. Fewer than 5 points refuses 'too-few'. A non-finite value, unequal lengths, an x that does not increase or a non-positive limit throws RangeError.

legs.what: y = 2 x + 1 on x = 0, 0.3, 1, 1.1, 2, 4.5, 5: both methods exact; y = x^2 on x = 0 to 8 in steps of 0.5: the linear error at every interior point is the square of the spacing
legs.bound: every error of the first at most 1e-12 in absolute value and closer 'tie'; every linear error of the second within 1e-12 of 0.25

legs.bound: every point's two errors absolute 1e-10; both RMS and both maxima absolute 1e-10; closer equal

amendments.text: Definitions the contract left open; no bound moved. (1) I1: the ledger also refuses 'non-finite' when an energy is not a finite number (a defensive refusal with no leg). (2) I1.a is evaluated with the exported explicit Euler step and the kernel's energy on one step, since the ledger refuses fewer than 8 steps. (3) The normals z of I3.b, I3.c and I4.d come from js/random/streams.js gaussian() on the named stream: for I3.b and I3.c one generator per series, drawn in time order; for I4.d from the same stream after its 60 uniforms, in time order after sorting. The series are written to inputs.json and the oracle reads them. (4) I4.f and I5.c: a row with a missing (non-finite) time, flux, mass or magnitude is dropped (I4.f: after taking every k-th row). (5) I5.c (ii): an age 'holds' a mass when the mass is inside its phase-0 mass range, ends included. (6) Module constant names (MIN_SERIES, MIN_TABLE) and extra returned fields (aliasRatio, warnings, pairs, errFixed) carry no bound.
